officialTitle: Durvalumab after Chemoradiotherapy in Stage III Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer

design.blinding: Placebo-controlled; PFS by blinded independent central review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Of 713 patients who underwent randomization, 709 received consolidation therapy (473 received durvalumab and 236 received placebo).
secondaryEndpoints: Time to death or distant metastasis
design.notes: 2:1 randomisation 1 to 42 days after platinum-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy without progression.

clinicalQuestion: Does consolidation durvalumab after platinum-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy improve PFS and OS in unresectable stage III NSCLC?

pico.population: Unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after two or more cycles of platinum-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy
pico.intervention: Durvalumab 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for up to 12 months
pico.outcomes: Co-primary: PFS (BICR) and OS. Secondary: ORR, time to death or distant metastasis, safety

arms.label: Durvalumab
arms.dosing: 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for up to 12 months
arms.doseSourceQuote: durvalumab (at a dose of 10 mg per kilogram of body weight intravenously) or placebo every 2 weeks for up to 12 months

publications.title: Durvalumab after Chemoradiotherapy in Stage III Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Primary PFS analysis

publications.title: Overall Survival with Durvalumab after Chemoradiotherapy in Stage III NSCLC.
publications.label: Overall survival analysis

publications.title: Five-Year Survival Outcomes From the PACIFIC Trial: Durvalumab After Chemoradiotherapy in Stage III Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: 5-year survival update

outcomes.endpointLabel: PFS by blinded independent central review
outcomes.sourceQuote: The median progression-free survival from randomization was 16.8 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 13.0 to 18.1) with durvalumab versus 5.6 months (95% CI, 4.6 to 7.8) with placebo (stratified hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.42 to 0.65; P<0.001)
The response rate was higher with durvalumab than with placebo (28.4% vs. 16.0%; P<0.001)

outcomes.endpointLabel: Time to death or distant metastasis
outcomes.sourceQuote: The median time to death or distant metastasis was longer with durvalumab than with placebo (23.2 months vs. 14.6 months; P<0.001).
Durvalumab significantly prolonged overall survival, as compared with placebo (stratified hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 99.73% CI, 0.47 to 0.997; P=0.0025).

The 24-month overall survival rate was 66.3% (95% confidence interval [CI], 61.7 to 70.4) in the durvalumab group, as compared with 55.6% (95% CI, 48.9 to 61.8) in the placebo group (two-sided P=0.005).
Estimated 5-year rates (95% CI) for durvalumab and placebo were 42.9% (38.2 to 47.4) versus 33.4% (27.3 to 39.6) for OS

safety.sourceQuote: Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 29.9% of the patients who received durvalumab and 26.1% of those who received placebo

safety.description: Grade 3 or 4 pneumonia (most common grade 3–4 event)
safety.sourceQuote: the most common adverse event of grade 3 or 4 was pneumonia (4.4% and 3.8%, respectively)

safety.description: Discontinuation of study drug due to adverse events
safety.sourceQuote: A total of 15.4% of patients in the durvalumab group and 9.8% of those in the placebo group discontinued the study drug because of adverse events.

strengths: Placebo-controlled randomised phase III with PFS and OS as co-primary endpoints
limitations: Randomisation after chemoradiotherapy excludes patients who progressed or could not complete concurrent treatment
Enrolled regardless of PD-L1 status, with subgroup questions unresolved by the abstract

clinicalImplications.text: Established consolidation durvalumab after concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy as the standard for unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression, with sustained survival benefit at five years.

tumourBoardPearl.text: PACIFIC eligibility starts after chemoradiotherapy — patients must be progression-free and recovered enough to begin durvalumab within the protocol window; EGFR-mutant disease is now addressed separately by LAURA.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstracts of PMIDs 28885881 (primary PFS), 30280658 (OS) and 35108059 (5-year update). Updated medians in the 5-year abstract are garbled in PubMed text and were not transcribed.
